 Aaron Tai-Roy King power into Japan Masters semi-finals
 13-Nov-2026, 12:43 13 Nov 2026, 12:43 K. Parkaran Share This marks the newly paired duo's third semi-final appearance in the five tournaments they have contested since teaming up last month.
 Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King beat Lee Jhe Huei-Yang Po Hsuan 21-16, 21-12 in just 28 minutes. 
 PETALING JAYA : Newly paired men’s doubles shuttlers Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King stormed into the semi-finals of the Japan Masters, making it their third last-four appearance in the five tournaments they had played since partnering last month. 
 World No 57 Aaron-Roy King, who lifted the Arctic Open title in their maiden outing last month, took just 28 minutes to dispose of Taiwan’s 15th-ranked duo Lee Jhe Huei-Yang Po Hsuan 21-16, 21-12 in the quarter-finals of the World Tour Super 500 championships.
 The duo had shocked their world No 5 compatriots Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani in straight games in the quarter-final yesterday.
 In the last-four match tomorrow, Aaron-Roy King will face either Danish pair Daniel Lundgaard-Mads Vestergaard or Japan’s Hiroki Okamura-Kyohei Yamashita.
 After winning the Arctic Open, the Badminton Association of Malaysia’s most successful experimental pair entered the semi-finals at the Hylo Open in Germany.
